svg.aria-label: AlcorBrowser: MCP broker + extension protocol, offline demo
svg.text: AlcorBrowser: MCP broker + extension protocol, offline demo

g.font-family: Cascadia Mono, Consolas, Menlo, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace
g.text: $ python AlcorBrowser/demo/run_demo.py
AlcorBrowser demo: real broker, real native host, pretend browser
== 1. Install into a temporary home, configure two agents and an upload folder
installed extension build b893f0342911 into extension-agents-demo
broker listening on a free loopback port
== 2. The pretend browser attaches through the real native host
PASS native host relayed hello -> welcome
PASS installed build matches the running one (no reload asked)
PASS broker lists one attached profile
== 3. Authentication and the browser-origin guard
PASS no token -> 401
PASS wrong token -> 401
PASS non-ASCII token -> a clean 401, not a crashed handler
PASS a web page's request (it carries an Origin) -> 403
PASS valid agent token -> 200
PASS the native relay's token is not an agent token
== 4. An agent drives the browser over MCP
server: alcor-browser 2.2.1
tools/list: 18 tools, e.g. browser_status, browser_restart, browser_tabs, browser_open, browser_focus, brows
er_navigate, ...
PASS tools/list exposes the browser tools
browser_open -> tab t1 (Sign in)
PASS browser_open names the tab with a short handle
e1 link "Home" -> /
e2 textbox "Email" editable
e3 textbox "Password" password editable
e4 button "Sign in"
f1 file-input accept="*"
PASS the snapshot flags the password field
(the password rule lives in extension/page.js; the fake page re-implements it)
... (73 lines omitted) ...
PASS refused: a manifest that drops the extension's own manifest.json
== 11. A failure while replacing files rolls everything back
check -> {'ok': False, 'failed': 'apply'}
PASS the apply step failed
PASS the backup was restored
PASS the tree is byte-identical to before the attempt
PASS the exit hook was not called for a failed update
47/47 checks passed
What this proved: agents authenticate per name; a browser page cannot reach the broker;
tools cross the real native-messaging path; the password floor's refusal travels back;
receipts hold hashes and origins, never text; uploads obey an allowlist and one-time
tickets; a timeout is 'uncertain' and never replayed; updates are verified, staged,
backed up and rolled back on failure. What it did not prove: the extension's JavaScript
in a real Chrome (see README, Scope and limits).
